ImageDescription.value: Photograph of Ranikhet from the Macnabb Collection (Col James Henry Erskine Reid): Album of views of 'Naini Tal' taken by Lawrie & Co in 1895. Ranikhet (Queen's Field) was named after a legendary Queen who camped in the area and fell in love with it. Situated 49 miles north of Nainital, the town provides a spectacular view of the Himalayan range. Ranikhet is still a military cantonment and the Kumaon Regiment has been stationed there from 1780. This is a General view of the hill station of Ranikhet, with snowy peaks in the distance.

ImageDescription.value: This image captures the serene beauty of Rani Jheel, a peaceful man-made lake located in Ranikhet, Uttarakhand. Surrounded by lush pine and deodar forests, the lake offers a quiet escape from the hustle of everyday life. The calm water reflects the greenery around it, and the small hanging bridge in the background adds a rustic charm. Visitors can enjoy boating, nature walks, and simply soaking in the scenic silence that makes this spot a hidden gem in the hills.
